title: observability-sync-sprint-bridge-2026-07-09
content:
Context and purpose:
This doc captures the Observability weekly sync for the sprint bridge (Mon 2026-07-06 -> Fri 2026-07-10). Focus areas: tracing sampling experiment, dashboard consolidation sprint, cost-telemetry anomaly detector spike, and ops runbook touchpoints for Dedicated capacity.

Attendees:
- Rae Chen (chair)
- Aisha Mendes
- Diego Alvarez
- Priya Kapoor
- Jonah Park
- Guests: Mei Lin (SRE), Carlos Ribeiro (Serving Runtime)

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Tracing sampling experiment v1 completed: 15% overall tail latency reduction for trace ingestion pipeline; sampling rules improved signal/noise ratio for cold-start traces.
- Dashboard consolidation MVP ready for QA: three overlapping dashboard panels removed; single-per-route latency heatmap added.
- Cost-telemetry anomaly detector spike: promising precision (~0.76) on historical incidents, but recall low for short-lived bursts—need more feature engineering.
- Runbook updates: added fallback escalation for Dedicated GPU pool OOMs; clarified owner rotations and Slack incident channel naming.

Detailed notes:
1) Tracing sampling experiment (owner: Diego)
- What we ran: rule-based pre-ingest sampling that keeps 100% of error traces and 20% of successful traces where time_to_first_token > 200ms; prefix-preserve for conversational sessions.
- Dataset: 30 days of production traces (June) replayed to local staging ingestion.
- Results:
  - Ingestion throughput up ~28% during peak windows.
  - Observed 15% lower median trace processing latency and 3x lower CPU load on the ingester farm for the same QPS.
  - Storage delta: net -36% index size for traces kept.
- Caveats and open questions:
  - Some important multi-request sessions lost fidelity when per-request sampling omitted early context (issue tracked JIRA-INF-2162).
  - Need to validate downstream APM dashboards still compute session-level metrics correctly.
- Immediate action items:
  - Diego to iterate on a lightweight session-reconstruction tag (due 2026-07-16).
  - Instrument additional trace attributes (kv_cache_hit, routing_policy) before sampling (Priya).

2) Dashboard consolidation sprint (owner: Aisha)
- Goal: reduce duplicate panels across infra/product dashboards and add a single, canonical per-route latency heatmap.
- Work completed:
  - Removed 9 duplicate panels from infra-dash and product-latency.
  - Introduced per-route heatmap panel for 50/90/99 latency with hover-to-filter.
  - Migrated cheaper queries (pre-aggregates) into a new 'dashboard-query-pool' to reduce cost.
- Observed impact:
  - Dashboard render time 40% faster for heavy dashboards.
  - Query cost for the consolidated dashboard decreased ~22% in the last 48h (sampling window).
- Blockers:
  - UX polish required: hover filters are slow in Safari (Mei to follow up).
- Next steps:
  - Aisha to schedule a UX walk-through with product on 2026-07-12.
  - Jonah to add dashboard smoke-check CI job (ticket JIRA-INF-2179).

3) Cost-telemetry anomaly detector spike (owner: Priya)
- Objective: prototype a lightweight anomaly detector for per-model cost spikes (token spend rate anomalies) that can surface to Alerts and Slack.
- Approach: ensemble of z-score on rolling window + seasonal decomposition + simple gradient-checker for burst detection.
- Evaluation: ran against 12 months of billing/telemetry; the prototype captured 8/10 known incidents (precision 0.76, recall 0.62).
- Failure modes: short, high-amplitude bursts (1–3 minutes) were frequently missed; noise from scheduled heavy batch jobs caused false positives.
- Proposed mitigations:
  - Add job-calendar filter (ingest from scheduling service) to suppress known bulk jobs.
  - Add short-window sensitivity toggle for high-frequency lanes (e.g., dedicated pools).
- Action items:
  - Priya to draft an RFC for detector thresholds and suppression rules (due 2026-07-20).
  - Diego to expose scheduler metadata in the cost-telemetry pipeline (INF-2187).

4) Ops/runbook updates for Dedicated (owner: Jonah)
- Updated steps for Dedicated GPU pool OOMs: include immediate pod-bounce checklist and memory pressure markers to record.
- Added a new escalation path: on repeated OOMs within 10m, automatically trigger fallback routing to lower-tier model (if configured).
- Runbook acceptance criteria: must be executable in <8 minutes by on-call SRE.
- Action: Jonah to run a tabletop on 2026-07-14 with SRE and Dedicated product owners.

5) Engineering standup items (shallow rollup):
- Rae: coordinate with Console team on per-token cost panel (blocked on backend index change).
- Aisha: finalize dashboard QA checklist; remove two more low-value panels next sprint.
- Diego: session-reconstruction tag spike; validate with tracing team.
- Priya: RFC for cost-detector; run additional backtests on spikes.
- Jonah: dashboard CI job + runbook tabletop.

Risks and escalations:
- If sampling removes session context, we risk breaking SLO-derived alerts and regressions in model-quality investigations. Mitigation: preserve minimal session head metadata and run A/B tests for 2 weeks before rollout.
- Detector false positives could erode trust—start with a low-noise alert channel (ops-only) and only escalate to paging after confirmed recurrence.

Decisions made:
- Proceed to limited canary of tracing sampling rules on 10% of traffic next week (owner Diego).
- Dashboard consolidation will prioritize query-cost reductions over visual parity; default to single-source-of-truth panels.

Open parking lot items:
- Long-term: consider adopting reservoir sampling for trace sessions (research item).
- Follow-up: evaluate cost-telemetry detector as a managed feature for Dedicated customers (commercial/contract implications).

Meeting artifacts and references:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/trace-sampling-experiments
- Jira: JIRA-INF-2145 (dashboard consolidation), JIRA-INF-2162 (trace sampling context), JIRA-INF-2187 (scheduler metadata)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/432 (query-pool implementation)

Immediate todo list (owners and dates):
- Diego: rollout canary to 10% traffic (2026-07-13).
- Priya: RFC for anomaly detector thresholds (2026-07-20).
- Aisha: UX walk-through and dashboard QA (2026-07-12).
- Jonah: add dashboard smoke CI job (2026-07-16) and runbook tabletop (2026-07-14).

Notes to self:
- Keep an eye on dataset skew when sampling is active; add a daily report for sample-retention stats.
- Capture a short postmortem if canary causes >5% lost session traces that impact SLOs.

End of notes.
